outline.rationale: The user is a total beginner wanting a solid conceptual understanding at the informed-layperson level, not to build models. I start with definitional grounding ("What is AI"), then the foundational mechanism (machine learning), then the technical leap (neural networks) since modern AI depends on it, then the most culturally relevant application (LLMs/chatbots) which is likely their main exposure point. I include capabilities/limits and ethics because these are central to genuinely "following conversations" about AI — a stated goal. Everyday uses make it concrete and relatable. History is placed last as context rather than a prerequisite. I deliberately excluded any coding, math, or hands-on model-building nodes since the user explicitly wants conceptual understanding over implementation. Nodes are MECE-ish: each answers a distinct question with low overlap.
